haiku-low.q1: Step 4, after build and lint pass, before new instances start. The live release must keep working on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, once the release still using it is retired.
haiku-low.q3: Pass the health gate and smoke suite by T0 + 10 minutes. If not, abort via step 8; the listener is untouched.
haiku-low.q4: All user traffic moves in one listener update that repoints the forward action to the new target group, with no weights.
haiku-low.q5: A window above 1% 5xx with at least 100 responses. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour and sets live_colour; migrations stay, hold_until unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: 30 minutes (the hold). After shutdown, rollback is a normal approved deploy of previous_release_digest, started by an engineer.
haiku-low.q7: Finished migrations stay applied; a failed transactional one is rolled back. Status is migration_failed, the lock is released, and the live colour keeps serving.
haiku-low.q8: Listener is the source of truth; state's live_colour must match it. Idle is the other colour, recorded as idle_colour in the state record.
haiku-low.q9: The state record's lock, set in step 1 and cleared in step 8 or 14. It is held through the whole 30-minute hold.
haiku-low.q10: The CI runner runs the smoke suite against each new instance through an internal test path, not the public listener.
haiku-low.q11: A one-off migration task from image_digest, in step 4. A PostgreSQL advisory lock stops two migrators running at once; the step runs once per deploy.
haiku-low.q12: Abort scales them to 0. After rollback, the new colour runs until hold_until, then stops. Next deploy's step 2 scales leftover idle instances to 0.

sonnet.q1: Migrations are applied in step 4, after build/test and before any new-release instances start. The live (old) release must keep working on the migrated schema, which is why migrations are additive only.
sonnet.q2: In a later release, once the release that still uses the column or table is retired.
sonnet.q3: It must pass the health gate (all 4 instances with 3 consecutive /healthz passes) and the smoke suite (run via internal test paths), both by T0 + 10 minutes. If not, the deploy aborts via step 8: the idle colour is scaled to 0, the listener is untouched, and the lock is released.
sonnet.q4: With one update to the public listener's forward action, repointing it to the new target group. There are no weights, so there is no gradual shift. The pipeline reads the listener back to confirm.
sonnet.q5: A breach is a 5xx rate strictly above 1% over a trailing window of min(5 min, time since switch) with at least 100 responses, found while status is watching (switch to watch_until, 15 min). The rollback repoints the listener to the old target group, sets live_colour to the old colour, and sets status to holding. It records rolled_back_from and stops the 5xx watch. It leaves the new colour running until hold_until, leaves hold_until unchanged, and does not reverse migrations. The lock stays held.
sonnet.q6: For 30 minutes (the hold, until hold_until). A manual rollback is available in that period (step 12, engineer-started and approved, when status is holding). After the old colour is shut down, a problem is handled by a normal deploy of previous_release_digest (steps 1 to 14 with the stated changes), started by an engineer with approval.
sonnet.q7: Migrations that finished before the failure stay applied, which is safe because they are additive. A failed transactional migration is rolled back by the database. Any INVALID index is dropped by the next deploy's migration task. The rest of the deploy stops: status becomes migration_failed, the lock is released, no new-release instances start, and the live colour keeps serving.
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads the public listener's forward target and maps it to a colour. That colour must match live_colour in the state record, and the other colour is idle_colour and gets the new release. The listener is the source of truth. idle_colour and release_sha are then recorded in the state record, catalog-web/<env>/deploy-state. A mismatch stops the deploy.
sonnet.q9: A lock in the state record (the deploy_id of the one running deploy), taken by CAS in step 1. A merge that finds it held writes its SHA to queued_sha and ends. The lock is held from step 1 until step 8 (abort) or step 14 releases it, so on a successful switch that includes the whole 30-minute hold. Steps 2, 3 and 4 also release it when they fail.
sonnet.q10: The CI runner runs the smoke suite against each new instance through its internal test path, a private per-instance address reachable from the pipeline's network. The public listener is not used and still forwards only to the live colour.
sonnet.q11: A one-off migration task run from image_digest in step 4. It takes a named PostgreSQL advisory lock, so only one migrator runs at a time. Within a deploy it runs once, in a single step. The migration tool's own table records which migrations have run, so applied ones are not repeated.
sonnet.q12: After an abort, the idle colour's desired count is set to 0 and its logs stay in the log system. If the scale-down fails, it is retried and then an alert is sent, and the next deploy's step 2 scales any running idle instances to 0 and waits for them to stop. After a rollback, the new colour keeps running as the non-live colour until hold_until, then step 13 shuts it down. The lock stays held until then, so the next deploy waits. If that colour was rolled back from, it must come back through a new deploy.
